page.layout: Two printed pages side by side, each with one wide column of running text, entries set in paragraphs. Left page: one column, with line numbers 10 to 60 at its inner edge. Right page: one column, continuing from the left page. Running head at the top of both pages. Page number 171 at top right. A printer's signature at the foot, centre right.

main_text.p: Dionysij Longini opuscula de magnitudine ôrationis, & de aciebus bellicis, & [illegible, ~12 letters] liber imperfectus, Græcè seruantur Romæ & Venetijs, & in Gallia. Liber de magnitudine orationis Græcè & Latinè impressus extat.

✦ Dionysius Metathemenus appellatus, Stoicus primò philosophus, verum cum in oculorum dolorem incidisset, à Zenone defecit, & ad Cyrenai cos se contulit, voluptatem finem dicens, scripsit De sedatione perturbationum lib.2. De exercita 10 tione 2. De voluptate 4. De diuitijs, & gratia & cruciatu. De hominum vsu. De felicitate. De animi tiquis regibus. De his quæ laudantur. De barba ricis consuetudinibus. Laertius.
Dionysius Milesius historicus, scripsit de rebus gestis post Darium libros 5. Descriptione orbis, Persica sermone Ionico, Troicorum libros tres, Mythica, Cyclum historicum libris 7. Suidas.
Dionysius Mitylenæus, verficator, Scythobrachio & Sutor dictus: descripsit Bacchi & Minervæ 20 expeditionem, Argonautas libris sex soluta oratione, Fabulosa ad Parmenonem. Suidas.
Dionysius Olynthius, vetustissimus scriptor, citatur à Tatiano.
Dionysius Siciliæ tyrannus, scripsit tragœdias & comœdias, & historica. Suidas.

Dionysius Siculi tyranni filius, & ipse tyrannus ac philosophus, reliquit epistolas, & librum de carminibus Epicharmi. Suidas. Athenæus cit. 30 at Dionysij tyranni Adonin & epistolas, incertum autem est an patris an filij fuerint.

Dionysij cuiusdam comœdia, Legislator, citatur ab Athenæo libro 9. Videdum an Sinopensis ab Siculi tyrani fuerit: Idè inter Opsartyticorum scriptores Dionysiū numerat, ac forte idè est qui & comœdia scripsit, nam versibus illis quos 39 opi nor adducit, coquus arte suam laudib. celebrat.
✦ Dionysius quidam Philadelphus, propter styli ac sermonis improprietatem vocatus Diacenus, 40 fertur author esse [illegible, ~10 letters], quæ Dionysio Alexandrino seu Afro inscribuntur.

page.notes: Left-page entries run into the right page at "De beneficijs". Line numbers 10 to 60 stand at the inner edge of the left page and are kept inline. Greek passages in the first entry and in the Dionysius Philadelphus entry are not legible at this scan resolution. Running head read as DIO on both pages. Some lib. numbers and title abbreviations in the right column are uncertain; the scan is soft there. The printer's signature "P 4" is read from a faint mark at the foot.
